newsitem.title: CHINA: China steel firm says no impact on Hong Kong units.
newsitem.headline: China steel firm says no impact on Hong Kong units.

text.p: Listed subsidiaries of China's Capital Iron and Steel Corp (Shougang) in Hong Kong were not affected by a recent restructuring of the steel giant, a company official said on Monday.
But the official told Reuters the overhaul that turned the company into a business group could have implications in the future.
"Currently, there has been no change made to those listed firms," the official said.
"It is hard to say whether there will be any changes in the future, but so far, there is no change," he said. "Their capital structures and relations with Shougang are still the same."
Shougang said on Saturday it was transformed into a business group with 27 subsidiaries under a parent company.
It also would gradually abandon financial subsidies given to its subsidiaries.
The moves coincided with the handing down of a suspended death sentence to Zhou Beifang, the former head of two of the Hong Kong-listed companies, in a major corruption scandal.
The official media announced the restructuring but did not report the sentencing.
The 27 subsidiaries included the China Shougang International Trading and Engineering Corp, which holds interests of four listed companies in Hong Kong, the official said.
The companies are Shougang Concord International Enterprises Co Ltd, Shougang Concord Grand (Group) Ltd, Shougang Concord Technology Holdings Ltd and Shougang Concord Century Holdings Ltd.
The group registered 1.653 billion yuan ($199 million) in pre-tax profits in the first 10 months of 1996, state media has said, without giving comparative figures.
